rationale: Evidence: iteration 6 (score 937.1, best so far) is the only design where every development track finished 20/20: oval 944.7, s-bend 940.9, slalom 925.7 with 0.65 line-loss events. The later single-variable tests all scored lower. Iteration 7 (y=0.07, kd 1.1) scored 930.9 and iteration 8 (kd 0.9) scored 865.3, with slalom falling to 13/20. Iteration 9 (kd 1.1 at y=0.06) scored 925.9, with slalom line loss and max_error both slightly worse than iteration 6. So kd 1.0 at y=0.06 is the local optimum I have measured. Iteration 4 showed that kp 6 collapses the oval and s-bend, and mass is already at its 0.40 kg floor. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit because the 0.06 m floor binds. Changes: none. I resubmit the iteration 6 design unchanged, because it is the most robust candidate on the three development tracks and the final track is unseen, so robustness matters more than a small gain. Expected result: about 937 on the development tracks, with 60/60 finishes. Hypotheses for later: (a) a modest base_speed increase (1.5 to about 1.6) would cut slalom time (2.92 s) and time is worth about 20 points per second, but it risks more slalom off-track exits; (b) line-loss events remain the largest recoverable term at about 15 points per event on slalom. Measurements wanted: per-track completion, max_error, line_loss_events, completion_time and steering_oscillation on all three tracks, to confirm the baseline is reproduced.
